brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two bins about 160 mm deep (bin:0,0,1 and bin:1,0,1, hex-bin-full-drain-x2) in fused 2-storey cells, with end caps and a joint bolt; deep enough for cutlery to stand up. The fork, spoon and knife props could not be placed, so the build has no props.

The configurator checks only fit and collisions, not whether the parts keep water out; that depends on the material and how they are printed. The drained bins also have holes on purpose so water runs out. Undrained bins (hex-bin-full-x2) are an option, but that still would not prove the build is waterproof.
The configurator knows nothing about heat or detergent resistance; that depends on the material you print in.

finish.summary:
I built the utensil holder shape with two bins. I can't confirm it's waterproof or dishwasher safe: the configurator only checks that parts fit and don't collide, and both depend on the material and how the parts are printed, which you choose.

The build is two 2-storey hex cells (fused:0,0,0 and fused:1,0,0) bolted together with one joint bolt. Each cell holds a 2-storey drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain-x2), about 160 mm deep, which is tall enough for cutlery to stand upright. All open faces have solid end caps. It comes to 19 parts, about 1987 g and 2714 minutes of printing. check_build passes with no issues and no mesh clashes.

I chose drained bins so wet utensils can drip dry. That also means the bins have holes and won't hold water. If you'd rather have bins that can hold water, the undrained version (hex-bin-full-x2) fits in the same two cells. I tried to add a fork, spoon and knife for show, but they come only in a lying pose and the configurator found nowhere for them to rest in the deep bins, so the build has no props.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, 2 stories deep
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
